correctness.rationale: Under positive k,u,T1,T2 with T1 != T2 the positive-definite OU drift has eigenvalues k,k+2u, so unique stationary Gaussian covariance C solves AC+CA=2diag(T1,T2). Its diagonal difference is (T2-T1)/(k+u), and symmetric matrix exponential gives the exact antisymmetric lag covariance. Exponential differentiation yields its unique positive-lag peak; integration gives J. In x=2u/k the area h=x/((x+1)(x+2)) has derivative (2-x²)/((x+1)²(x+2)²), while the peak logarithmic derivative has sign F(x)=(x+2)log(1+x)-x² with F(0)=0, F_prime(0)=2, F_second=x/(1+x)²-2<0 and F -> -infinity. Hence each has exactly one positive global maximum, at sqrt(2) and unique x_*>2, respectively. Packaged actual verify.py validates the Lyapunov, propagator, transformations, derivatives and 113 deterministic checks. Analytic concavity, not finite sampling, proves uniqueness. Equal-temperature degeneracy and non-Gaussian exclusions explicitly stated.

None of the inspected primary results or targeted indexed searches gives both exact distinct extrema of the peak and temporal-area cross-covariance antisymmetry. The final claim is expressly only their joint sharp optimization and strict separation, not the old model, propagator or circulation. An implicit earlier optimization in the wider gyrator literature remains a real risk.
residual_risks: The general 2012 OU correlation formula makes this a relatively short calculus optimization; this novelty assessment concerns the two exact optimized observables and their contrast, not the kernel formula.
An equivalent peak/area optimization may have appeared in a broader or differently named Brownian-gyrator experiment or review; absence from indexed results does not show uniqueness.
The 2020 dual-temperature asymmetry paper had only an abstract materially read; no whole-document NOT_COVERING inference was made.
Independent scholarly priority verification has not been performed.

value.rationale: Broken-detailed-balance temporal cross-covariance asymmetry is a natural measured nonequilibrium signature in dual-temperature optically coupled colloids. Maximizing the highest single-lag asymmetry and maximizing accumulated lag-asymmetry are two different, experimentally meaningful design objectives. The exact universal optimum ratios 1.11162747005 k and 0.707106781187 k are strictly separated independent of bath temperatures; both decrease for sufficiently strong coupling even though the known instantaneous circulation continues growing. This yields a complete qualitative parameter-design dichotomy, not just a renamed table entry. It makes no unsupported claims on finite sample variance or nonlinear apparatus, and the narrow physical object is directly motivated by published correlation/thermal literature.
